propositions: The `transition` command has two distinct force flags with different meanings: `--force` for start-work gate bypass and `--force-close` for completion gate bypass, while `claim` uses `--force[=<reason>]`, creating spelling inconsistency.

The proposed rename collapses `transition`'s two force flags into one `--force[=<reason>]` with dispatch by target status: on `open -> in_progress` it bypasses start-work gate, and on close it bypasses completion gate with optional reason.

A clean break without deprecation alias is required; the parser must explicitly reject the retired `--force-close` spelling with a CommandError rather than silently skip it, preventing silent no-ops on stale invocations.

The library kwarg `rebar.transition(..., force_close=...)` and internal Python identifiers retain their names; only the CLI flag string `--force-close` is renamed to `--force`, and `transition_compute` gains a `force_reason` keyword for explicit audit notes.

A concurrent change (`scripts/dependency_audit.py` from ticket 63e8) introduced a new emitter of the retired `--force-close` flag post-merge, requiring a regression test that feeds generated argv to the real `_parse_flags` to catch future renames.

A tree-wide guard test ensures the old flag spelling appears only in frozen experimental corpora, CHANGELOG, release-notes, the parser's rejection branch, and its own test, preventing new stale references from silently accumulating.
